front: Thursday's four-game slate was settled by one game. Detroit beat Washington by 4 in overtime, and five of the night's seven best scores came from it: Cade Cunningham 80.5 (52 on 16-25 in 48 minutes), Ausar Thompson 61.7 (17-11-11 with 6 stocks), Trae Young 56.4 (37 and 14 assists), Anthony Davis 55.0 and Alex Sarr 50.8 (30 on 12-14). Minnesota beat Dallas by 39, which sank Flagg (28.9), Kyrie, Washington and Gafford, and Barnes and LeBron were ruled out after your 5:10am lock, so Toronto and Philadelphia sit out the morning's grading. Your 80 teams had a median finish in the top 46%; 8 made the top 10% (the field's rate), none the top 1% (best top 1.2%), and 19 cashed, returning $234 on $400: below average, not a disaster. Your memory is mostly right, with two exceptions. You were light on Cade (11 of 80 teams, against a sixth of the field), Sarr (6) and Trae in the afternoon (2 of 40), and on Murray-Boyles in the morning (2 of 40). But Ausar was your second-biggest bet (29 of 80, 48% of your morning teams), and his holders made the top 10% three times as often as the field. You were also over the field on Murray-Boyles in the afternoon (10 of 40, against 16%). Where the fades came from: in the afternoon you put Flagg ahead of Cade, Embiid ahead of Trae, Edgecombe and Kyshawn George ahead of Ausar, and Robinson ahead of Sarr, and all five moves lost. The overtime itself couldn't be seen coming. The repeatable part is the season pattern: fading a player who then plays 4+ minutes over his usual is now 9 right and 22 wrong, and your biggest overweights, Diabate (40% of your teams) and Reid (34%), both came in a little under the field's rate (0.9 and 0.8 times). Nothing to decide today.

moves.3: Every morning role call in this tier ran into Quickley, who scored 46 in his second game back from the hamstring: the button had him ahead of George, Bridges, Gobert and Washington, and the button was right.
